Read a NumPy file

Source: R/read.R
npy_read.Rd

Reads a .npy or .npz file from a path, a URL or a connection, and decodes it as npy_decode() does.

Usage

npy_read(file, ..., names = NULL, max_size = 2 * 1024^3)

Arguments

file

A path, a URL (http://, https://, ftp://, ftps:// or file://), or a connection.

...

Further arguments of npy_decode(): order, int64, na, strings, encoding, datetime, max_header, max_dims and max_members.

names

For a .npz, the members to read (by default all of them).

max_size

The largest input accepted, in bytes.

Value

As npy_decode().

Details

The input is read whole into memory first, never more than max_size bytes of it: a path whose size is above max_size is refused before it is opened, and a URL or connection is read no further than one byte past it. For a .npz, names decodes and inflates only the members named.

A connection that is not open is opened in binary mode and closed again; an open one must be binary, is read from its current position, and is left open.

See also

npy_write(); npy_header() and npy_names() read only the header or the directory.

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".npy")
npy_write(matrix(1:6, 2), f)
npy_read(f)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    1    3    5
#> [2,]    2    4    6
unlink(f)
